content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I am working with a [product_no] together with an 8 GB SD card for a solar application. I noticed, as the manual explains, that it only saves 2000 lines of data per file and then overwrites the existing file, instead of creating a new file once the memory limit is reached. Is there a way to make it generate a new file each time it reaches the 2000 line limit? It seems inefficient that the [product_no] supports an 8 GB SD card but cannot store more than 2000 lines without starting a new file. Regards, [user_name]
Try connecting your [product_name] to the internet and consider using one of the logging options mentioned at [url].

Hello, Unfortunately, you cannot make use of all the SD card's memory. The logging feature works, but it is not optimally implemented in the firmware. You can only address this limitation by using external logging software. Best regards, [user_name]

Thank you for the replies. It appears that 8 GB card support doesn't actually benefit users! I read that if the program is stopped and restarted, the device generates a new log file. My question is how to program it to stop and start without external intervention. For example, if I use a timer to power off the device for a short period, would this be considered stopping the program? Best regards, [user_name]

Hello, This topic was discussed in the German section of the forum and the conclusion was: it's not possible! However (I have no [product_name] available to test), perhaps you could use one output relay to interrupt the device's power supply through programming, but you'd need to adapt other program functions as well. Best regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: Forum users highlight major restrictions in the data logging functionality of the [product_no] when using large SD cards. Despite support for 8 GB cards, the device's firmware limits each file to 2000 lines and overwrites files instead of creating new ones. This limitation prevents users from continuous data logging in solar applications, creating frustration due to unutilized storage potential.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the device to fully utilize large SD card capacity by generating new data files once 2000 lines are reached. They seek a solution that allows for ongoing data logging without repeatedly overwriting existing files.
